Earnings Call Transcript
LivaNova (LIVN) Q4 2025 Earnings Call Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

Updated Feb 25, 2026 at 12:37PM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


Date
Feb. 25, 2026, 8 a.m. ET
Call participants
Chief Executive Officer and Director — Vladimir Makatsaria
Chief Financial Officer — Alex Shvartsburg
Chief Innovation Officer — Ahmet Tezel
Vice President, Investor Relations — Briana Gotlin
Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email
[email protected]
Takeaways
Group revenue
-- $361 million for the quarter, representing 9.5% constant currency and organic growth versus 2024.
Full-year revenue
-- Double-digit revenue growth and the fifth consecutive year of double-digit EPS growth.
Cardiopulmonary revenue
-- $207 million for the quarter (up 10%); $785,000,000 for the year (up 13%).
Heart-lung machine (HLM) growth
-- Full-year revenue grew in the mid-teens, with ESSENCE placements accounting for about 55% of annual units in 2025.
Cardiopulmonary consumables
-- Revenues rose in the mid-teens for the quarter and low-teens for the year, driven by market share gains, procedure growth, and pricing.
Epilepsy segment revenue
-- Quarter revenue rose 9%, Europe and Rest of World up 17%, U.S. up 8% year over year; full-year revenue up 6% (Europe/ROW up 13%, U.S. up 5%).
Adjusted gross margin
-- 68% for the quarter, consistent with 2024, with mix and pricing gains offset by currency and tariffs.
Adjusted SG&A expense
-- $131 million (36% of revenue), down from 38% in 2024 due to fixed cost leverage.
Adjusted R&D expense
-- $49 million (14% of revenue), up mainly from higher OSA and core development spend.
Adjusted operating income
-- $64 million (margin 18%), versus $56 million and 17% last year; increases from growth and cost leverage, partially offset by capacity and R&D investments.
Adjusted EPS
-- $0.86 for the quarter, up from $0.81 in 2024, with $0.04 favorable impact from timing of ESSENCE-related costs.
Cash position
-- $636 million at year-end, up from $429 million, due to operating cash flow and release of $295,000,000 restricted cash from SNIA litigation guarantee termination.
Total debt
-- $377 million at year-end, down from $628 million, following early repayments.
Adjusted free cash flow
-- $53 million for the quarter (down from $62 million prior year) and $183 million for the full year (up from $163 million), with the quarterly decline due to higher capital spend.
2026 revenue guidance
-- Forecast of 6%-7% constant currency growth, with Cardiopulmonary expected at 7%-8% and Epilepsy at 5.5%-6.5% (U.S. mid-single digits, Europe/ROW high single digits).
2026 EPS guidance
-- Adjusted diluted earnings per share projected at $4.15-$4.25 (about 8% growth at midpoint), including a $0.06 EPS drag for a third-quarter SNIA payment.
2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance
-- Expected $160 million–$180 million, with $120 million capital spend incorporated.
Medicare reimbursement
-- For VNS Therapy, outpatient payments to hospitals increase by about 48% for new implants and 47% for end-of-service procedures starting Jan. 1, 2026.
FDA and clinical milestones
-- Received approval for the cloud-based digital health platform in Epilepsy; full market release of the Bluetooth-enabled pulse generator in 2027.
OSA regulatory timeline
-- Modular PMA for clinical trial device progressing; first half 2026 approval expected, MRI-compatible commercial device supplement to follow, limited release in 2027, with broader launch in second half 2027.
Leadership addition
-- Lucille Blaze appointed as Global Head of Commercialization for obstructive sleep apnea.
Debt reduction actions
-- Early repayment of $200,000,000 term facilities and $58,000,000 convertible notes; full repayment of remaining term facilities in Jan. 2026.
Summary
LivaNova

(
LIVN

+2.37%
)
management highlighted strategic progress in both core and pipeline businesses, with clear direction on entering high-growth segments such as obstructive sleep apnea and digital health for neuromodulation. Company executives stressed durable market share and profit gains in core Cardiopulmonary and Epilepsy, attributing near-term commercial upside to upgraded reimbursement, large clinical studies, and product platform expansion. The company remains committed to execution, investing in advanced R&D across segments, digital capabilities with a newly FDA-approved platform, and scaling next-generation manufacturing, all while deleveraging its balance sheet and maintaining capital discipline.
Makatsaria said, entering higher-growth markets like OSA will shift LivaNova's overall weighted average market growth upward and position the company for sustained acceleration.
Shvartsburg flagged a 4 percentage point rise in the adjusted effective tax rate, noting, The increase was related to changes in geographic mix and the roll-off of certain tax attributes
Tezel confirmed, We continue to expect PMA approval for the clinical trial device in the first half of this year, followed by a PMA supplement for the commercial MRI-compatible device.
Management characterized reimbursement gains as a significant tailwind, noting that improved Medicare rates will meaningfully address prior hospital cost hurdles for VNS Therapy in the U.S.
Tezel described the OSPREY trial as the first and only randomized controlled trial in the HGNS space, confirming inclusion of challenging patient populations and citing responder rates comparable to less complex pivotal studies.
Industry glossary
VNS Therapy
: Implantable device delivering vagus nerve stimulation, primarily for drug-resistant epilepsy and difficult-to-treat depression.
ESSENCE
: LivaNova's advanced Heart-Lung Machine platform, signifying next-generation technology within the Cardiopulmonary segment.
HGNS
: Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation, a neurostimulation device class used for treating obstructive sleep apnea.
OSPREY trial
: LivaNova's randomized controlled trial evaluating HGNS therapy for OSA with broad inclusion criteria.
POLYSYNC
: LivaNova's advanced titration algorithm enabling multicontact activation in HGNS devices for personalized therapy optimization.
SNIA litigation guarantee
: A legal agreement whose termination released restricted cash on LivaNova's balance sheet.
DRE
: Drug-resistant epilepsy, a clinical subpopulation targeted by LivaNova's neuromodulation business.

We continue to view OSA as a very compelling de-risked opportunity, grounded in differentiated technology and clinical evidence, as well as our established neuromodulation capabilities. On the clinical evidence front, we expect a full 12-month dataset from the OSPREY trial to be published imminently. OSPREY is the first and only randomized controlled trial in the HGNS space, bringing gold standard scientific rigor to the field. As previously disclosed, patients with complete concentric collapse, or CCC, were not excluded from OSPREY, and approximately 45% of participants were high risk for this condition.
OSPREY also enrolled a challenging patient population with higher baseline AHI and BMI compared to other pivotal U.S. trials, yet the responder rates were comparable to these studies, even though other studies screened the more difficult-to-treat patients out. As a reminder, POLYSYNC is our advanced titration algorithm designed to fully leverage the six-electrode architecture of our HGNS cuff, which was not done in OSPREY. It enables multicontact activation for greater nerve and muscle selectivity, optimizing therapy for each patient.

We look forward to sharing the full POLYSYNC results at the SLEEP conference in June, but are confident we will be able to convert at least half of the nonresponders into responders using the POLYSYNC algorithm. As a reminder, we intend to make POLYSYNC immediately available during our commercial launch to ensure all of our patients have access to this advanced algorithm at their initial titration. This will not be used as a follow-up for nonresponders.
We will optimize therapy with POLYSYNC for all patients from the start.

Please go ahead.
Our next question comes from Michael K. Polark. Michael, please go ahead.
Morning. Maybe China. So can you be more specific on where that slipped, and if it is in China, your fresh perspective as it launches in China? Thank you.

Yeah. Mike, good morning. Good to hear from you. On the first part of the question, like Alex said, the shift in some placements was immaterial and will be fully captured, the majority in Q1 of this year and then potentially some in Q2. Regarding China, our launch is going as planned. We continue to be very optimistic about that market. Just a reminder, China is our second-largest market in terms of placed units. We are the market leader there, and our current win rate in China is above 80%. To give you a little flavor on the launch, we had the product approved in the first half of the year and a commercial launch in the second half.
Given the timing of the capital sales cycle, the first placement actually was in November. So 2025 was the year of preparation and launch, and 2026 will be the first year of significant impact with this launch in China. We see the funnel of new placements, and we are very confident in our ability to scale. As a reminder, ESSENCE, in terms of percent placements of all HLM, is going from approximately 55% last year to approximately 80% this year.

On the reimbursement increase, can you remind us how long the window is to get a replacement? I am imagining it is 12 months. I think I see evidence the device alerts that much in advance. And so could there be a dynamic…

We have fully contemplated the reimbursement change dynamics around end-of-service replacements in our planning. While devices do provide advance alerts, the timing of replacement procedures is driven by clinical scheduling and hospital workflows, and we expect a steady cadence rather than a sharp pull-forward.

qa_turns.speaker_name: And just to clarify a related topic on procedure coding that has come up recently
qa_turns.text:
historically, the previous-generation device of the HGNS incumbent was in a different code than VNS. When they moved into the latest generation, temporarily they began utilizing the VNS code for HGNS therapy as well. Consistent with CMS’s recent statements, we believe the code for VNS Therapy for Epilepsy should be separate and not shared with reimbursement codes for HGNS or OSA. As we prepare for our launch in OSA, we will continue to work with the relevant medical societies to have the most appropriate HGNS code. At launch, we will utilize the prevailing codes at that time.
Because the features and procedure for our HGNS technology are similar to the incumbent, we do not see risk of reclassification for VNS Therapy in Epilepsy. We believe VNS Therapy for Epilepsy and HGNS for OSA should have separate codes.
Alright. Super helpful. Thanks.
Our next question comes from Anthony Petrone with Mizuho Group. Anthony, please go ahead.

Thank you, and good morning, everyone. Congrats on a strong 2025. Question on RECOVER and one on R&D spend. When we think on RECOVER and depression, I know timing is still up for debate. But if we look ahead and take a glass half full approach, assuming that we get favorable coverage, I am wondering from the company's perspective, is favorable coverage now level 6 coding, that in depression we should expect that to code to level 6, and i.e., payout $45,000 or so on an outpatient basis versus what we estimate is a $25,000 device input cost? Or should we assume that still level 5 coding at $30,000 to $35,000 is still a best-case outcome?
And I have one quick question on R&D and R&D spend. Thanks.

I will comment on the code piece and then ask Alex to comment on pricing. We anticipate that depression would use the same code as VNS Therapy for Epilepsy. So whatever the VNS Therapy code is for Epilepsy, depression will be together with it.
I would just say it is too early to comment on ASPs, given that we are still awaiting the reimbursement decision from CMS.

Helpful. And then just R&D spend, Alex, it ticked up a little bit in Q4. I am just wondering what the complexion was there. Was that RECOVER manuscripts? Was it setting up sleep apnea? Something else that we are not seeing, device redesign, and is the fourth-quarter level for R&D sort of the new run rate?

Thanks. I will speak to R&D in general as it relates to 2026. We are largely maintaining our R&D investment in the core for 2026. We want to continue to advance innovation to fuel sustainable growth in both Epilepsy and Cardiopulmonary. In Epilepsy, we are prioritizing development of our next-generation Bluetooth-enabled IPG, which we intend to launch in 2027. In Cardiopulmonary, we are investing in the next-gen oxygenator and additional HLM hardware enhancements to strengthen our market leadership. The next-gen oxygenator is expected to launch in 2027–2028.

This year, we are increasing our investment in OSA product development. The investment is focused on our next-generation device, which will be the product that we launch into the market in 2027. Just as a reminder, our goal is to continue to drive adjusted operating margins above 20% annually despite ramping investments in the OSA business. Our 2026 guidance is very much in line with the targets we set.
Thank you.
The next question comes from Mike Matson with Needham & Co. Mike, please go ahead.

Thanks. Just with where things currently stand with the OSA HGNS reimbursement, assuming nothing changes there going into 2027 when you go into your full launch, what does that mean for that launch and that business for LivaNova PLC? Does it limit you somehow, or can it still be equally successful if reimbursement does not improve?

I will comment on the reimbursement piece. We are very comfortable with the current coding that CMS has guided toward. It will still be a very meaningful growth opportunity for us. Our excitement around the OSA space has not changed at all. We believe we have a differentiated technology with compelling clinical outcomes. This is a disease state with unmet needs; it is underdiagnosed, and the patient population is growing. Nothing has changed for us since the Investor Day in terms of our excitement.

Got it. And then just another one on sleep apnea. At Investor Day, you had spoken about making some investments in 2026. Can you talk about what you are doing this year to set the stage? Are you going to start hiring reps, and how much have you baked into the OpEx guidance to account for those investments this year?

On the R&D side, we have multiple key deliverables. One, we need to continue and finalize the POLYSYNC clinical work, and we are spending time and energy there. We are still actively working to get our clinical trial device approved; we expect that in the first half of this year. And we are actively working on our commercial launch device, the MRI-compatible version, which will be submitted after approval of the clinical trial version. On the commercial side, we will invest in 2026, but it is fairly limited this year. The broader build of commercial capabilities is more in 2027 onwards, as discussed at Investor Day. Nothing has changed compared to what we shared in November.
Thank you.
Our next question comes from John McAulay with Stifel. John, please go ahead.

Hi. Good morning. Just want to follow up on the earlier guidance questions. The last three years, by our math, you grew double digits. This year, you are saying 6% to 7%, albeit that is in line with the Investor Day guidance. I just want to be very clear that there is not any negative shift in dynamics reflected there, whether it be tougher comps or being later in the ESSENCE upgrade cycle. Is this truly just conservative positioning as you start the year?

John, thank you for the question. There is no negative dynamic. We are consistent with our guidance philosophy that we have had in past years. At Investor Day, I was asked what the biggest levers to the upside from our plan are, and they remain the same. We have to see how the reimbursement improvement and clinical data impact our Epilepsy business. On the Cardiopulmonary side, we are continuing to gain market share in oxygenators, and our ability to scale manufacturing faster will be an additional lever of growth.

I would just add that in our guidance we assumed a moderation in the price premium on ESSENCE relative to 2025, and we took a conservative stance on oxygenator output given third-party component supply constraints we have been working through. Those are the two elements that moderated our assumptions going into 2026.

qa_turns.speaker_name: That is very helpful color. And switching gears to Epilepsy
qa_turns.text: if I recall, something like 40% of your patient population is covered by Medicaid—you can correct that if the number is off—but my understanding is that reimbursement there for a decent portion of states has to be adjusted at the state level. Could you give us an update on where you are in terms of Medicaid reimbursement changes and where you might expect to be by the end of the year?

The way to think about this is Medicaid will essentially follow Medicare. While it will take some time to work through individual state processes, we assume that ultimately Medicaid will get to the same level of reimbursement.
Those are all the questions we have time for today, and so I will turn the call back over to Vladimir Makatsaria for closing remarks.
Well, thank you, everyone, for joining the call today, and thank you for your continued support and interest in LivaNova PLC, and have a good day ahead.
Bye.
Thank you everyone for joining us today.
